gaps.concept: Glucosuria causes osmotic diuresis, producing polyuria and polydipsia; insulin deficiency also causes catabolic weight loss and polyphagia.
gaps.why_tested: A patient presents with thirst, frequent urination, increased appetite, and unexplained weight loss.

gaps.concept: C-peptide reflects endogenous insulin secretion: it is low in established type 1 diabetes and often preserved in type 2 diabetes.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks whether an insulin-treated patient still produces insulin.

gaps.concept: Type 1 diabetes clusters with autoimmune thyroid disease, celiac disease, and Addison disease.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with diabetes develops another autoimmune disorder.

gaps.concept: Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults has islet autoantibodies and gradual beta-cell loss despite an initial type 2 appearance.
gaps.why_tested: An adult labeled with type 2 diabetes progressively requires insulin and has positive GAD antibodies.

gaps.concept: Gestational diabetes results from pregnancy-induced insulin resistance, particularly placental lactogen, and increases later type 2 diabetes risk.
gaps.why_tested: Hyperglycemia first appears during pregnancy and resolves after delivery.

gaps.concept: Chronic pancreatitis, cystic fibrosis, and hemochromatosis can cause diabetes through pancreatic damage.
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops diabetes alongside pancreatic disease or iron overload.

gaps.concept: Glucocorticoid exposure, Cushing syndrome, and acromegaly can cause secondary diabetes through insulin resistance.
gaps.why_tested: New hyperglycemia follows steroid treatment or accompanies excess cortisol or growth hormone.

gaps.concept: Without unequivocal symptomatic hyperglycemia, diabetes diagnosis requires two abnormal test results.
gaps.why_tested: An asymptomatic patient has one glucose or HbA1c value above the diagnostic threshold.

gaps.concept: Iron deficiency can falsely elevate HbA1c; altered red-cell turnover calls for plasma glucose testing.
gaps.why_tested: HbA1c conflicts with measured glucose in a patient with anemia.

gaps.concept: Fructosamine reflects glycemia over approximately two to three weeks and can assess control when HbA1c is unreliable.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with hemolysis needs a marker of recent glycemic control.

gaps.concept: Early diabetic nephropathy causes glomerular hyperfiltration from increased intraglomerular pressure before GFR declines.
gaps.why_tested: A newly diagnosed patient has elevated GFR despite emerging kidney injury.

gaps.concept: Diabetic nephropathy hyalinizes both afferent and efferent renal arterioles; efferent involvement distinguishes it from typical hypertensive nephrosclerosis.
gaps.why_tested: Renal histology asks which arteriole distinguishes diabetes from hypertension.

gaps.concept: Diabetic nephropathy also causes diffuse mesangial expansion and glomerular basement-membrane thickening.
gaps.why_tested: A renal biopsy shows diabetic injury without nodular glomerulosclerosis.

gaps.concept: Nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy features dot-blot hemorrhages, hard exudates, and cotton-wool spots without neovascularization.
gaps.why_tested: Fundus findings must be classified as nonproliferative or proliferative retinopathy.

gaps.concept: Proliferative retinopathy can cause vitreous hemorrhage and tractional retinal detachment.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with retinal neovascularization develops sudden vision loss.

gaps.concept: Diabetic macular edema results from retinal vascular leakage and causes central vision loss.
gaps.why_tested: A diabetic patient has reduced central vision with retinal thickening.

gaps.concept: Diabetic ischemic third-nerve palsy usually spares the pupil, unlike a compressive posterior communicating artery aneurysm.
gaps.why_tested: A diabetic patient develops ptosis and diplopia with preserved pupillary constriction.

gaps.concept: Diabetic neuropathy can cause Charcot arthropathy: a warm, swollen, relatively painless foot with bony destruction.
gaps.why_tested: Foot imaging shows joint collapse despite little pain.

gaps.concept: Diabetes accelerates atherosclerosis, increasing ischemic stroke and peripheral arterial disease as well as coronary disease.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with longstanding diabetes develops claudication or ischemic stroke.

gaps.concept: Hyperglycemia impairs neutrophil chemotaxis and phagocytosis, contributing to infection susceptibility.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks why infections are unusually frequent or severe in diabetes.

gaps.concept: Type 1 diabetes requires exogenous insulin; insulin's major adverse effects are hypoglycemia and weight gain.
gaps.why_tested: A newly diagnosed type 1 patient needs treatment, or an insulin-treated patient develops sweating and confusion.

gaps.concept: Rapid-acting insulin analogs cover meals; long-acting analogs provide basal insulin.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks which insulin replaces meal-related versus fasting secretion.

gaps.concept: Metformin reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis; adverse effects include gastrointestinal upset, vitamin B12 deficiency, and rare lactic acidosis.
gaps.why_tested: A type 2 patient starts first-line medication and develops diarrhea or otherwise unexplained neuropathy.

gaps.concept: Sulfonylureas close beta-cell ATP-sensitive potassium channels, increasing insulin release; they can cause hypoglycemia and weight gain.
gaps.why_tested: A type 2 patient develops hypoglycemia after starting a drug that requires functioning beta cells.

gaps.concept: GLP-1 receptor agonists increase glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppress glucagon, slow gastric emptying, and promote weight loss; nausea is common.
gaps.why_tested: A patient loses weight but develops nausea after starting injectable diabetes therapy.

gaps.concept: DPP-4 inhibitors prolong endogenous incretin activity and are generally weight-neutral with low hypoglycemia risk.
gaps.why_tested: A question contrasts an incretin-preserving drug with a GLP-1 receptor agonist.

gaps.concept: SGLT2 inhibitors block proximal-tubule glucose reabsorption, causing glucosuria; adverse effects include genital mycoses and euglycemic ketoacidosis.
gaps.why_tested: A treated patient has glucosuria, a genital yeast infection, or ketoacidosis with modest glucose elevation.

gaps.concept: Thiazolidinediones activate PPAR-gamma to improve insulin sensitivity; adverse effects include edema, heart-failure worsening, weight gain, and fractures.
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops edema after starting pioglitazone.

gaps.concept: Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors delay intestinal carbohydrate absorption and commonly cause flatulence and diarrhea.
gaps.why_tested: A diabetes drug blunts postprandial glucose excursions but causes gastrointestinal symptoms.

gaps.concept: Pramlintide is an amylin analog that suppresses glucagon and delays gastric emptying; combined with insulin, it can cause hypoglycemia.
gaps.why_tested: An insulin-treated patient receives an amylin analog for postprandial glucose control.
